news.blurb: Google DeepMind partners with game studios to prototype breakthrough AI gameplay.

news.title: Harvard’s $699 startup bootcamp offers AI avatars of its instructors
news.blurb: In the HBS Foundry program, AI avatars provide feedback during practice pitches and board meetings.

news.title: Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, says its AI ‘teammate’ just outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research
news.blurb: Built by DeepMind alumni, British AI lab Inherent released Faraday, an AI agent whose ability to replicate scientific papers could be a stepping stone for innovation.

news.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
news.blurb: OpenAI is calling for California to strengthen SB 53, an AI safety bill that the company previously opposed.

news.title: Frontier AI labs still won’t say how they’d contain a rogue model
news.blurb: A new study finds leading AI labs have few publicly documented plans for containing rogue models, raising questions about preparedness as AI systems increasingly demonstrate unexpected and potentially dangerous behavior.

news.title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
news.blurb: Anthropic forbids its Claude models from generating sexually explicit content. But a series of tests conducted by TechCrunch found that it didn't take much to get past the restriction.

news.title: Nvidia partners with data center developer Cloverleaf
news.blurb: Nvidia continues to pour money into data center development — just as AI data centers bring lots of money into Nvidia.

news.title: Over 1 million people have clicked LinkedIn’s AI slop button
news.blurb: LinkedIn actually announced a "Seems like AI slop" button on July 30th, and the company says that a lot of people have already used it. According to a Thursday post from chief product officer Hari Srinivasan, "over a million people" have clicked on the button, which is accessible from the three dots menu on a […]

news.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
news.blurb: Nvidia research shows that AI agents can perform well, and not go off the deep end, through fine-tuning, even if the AI model isn't that great at the task.
